nestedscales API

The language-neutral contract every binding implements. Each function has the same name and argument order in every language, and is called as a free function: scale_frames(s) in R and Julia, ns.scale_frames(s) in Python, nestedscales::scale_frames(s) in C++.

Correctness is checked against the R package: specs/goldens/generate.R writes the cases, and every binding replays them.

Type mapping

Concept R Python
scale S7 NestedScale frozen dataclass NestedScale
table data.frame / lazy arrow pyarrow.Table (accepts polars, pandas)
character vector character list[str] (a bare str is one element)
missing NULL / NA None
verdict with evidence logical + attribute offenders / sizes Verdict(ok, offenders, sizes); truthy, == bool
error stop() NestedScalesError (a ValueError)
warning warning() NestedScalesWarning
summary summary(x) scale_summary(x)
print print(x) str(x); repr(x) is the one-line format()
subclass hook S7 generic functools.singledispatch
source / target argument source / target source / target
named vector argument (rule = c(a = "sum")) named vector or list dict
lazy input arrow Dataset / dtplyr pyarrow.dataset.Dataset, polars LazyFrame
x[frame, unit] [.NestedScale x[frame, unit] (__getitem__)
dense array array with dimnames numpy.ndarray; labels are scale_units()

Rows of returned tables are sorted by code point in Python and by the session locale in R, so row order is not part of the contract. Code vocabularies (scale_units, children, parents) are in canonical member order everywhere.

Error and warning messages are kept verbatim across bindings.

Missing values follow R: an aggregate over a group containing a missing value is missing, and a target whose sources are only partly present in the data is missing (the partial-source law). A lazy input returns the observed target units only unless collect = TRUE; a materialised result is completed to the full target vocabulary, identifier groups in first-appearance order and target codes in member order, a missing-target row last.

Known differences:

  • a filtered scale whose codes are too long to list is named with a hash of them; R uses rlang::hash(), which cannot be reproduced outside R, so such names differ between bindings;
  • R’s YAML writer stores named numbers (coverage, parent_totals, a Calendar’s tokens) as bare sequences rounded to 7 digits; the Python reader maps them back onto the declared weights and recomputes coverage from the parent totals, and the Python writer stores named mappings at full precision.

Functions

Status: R = in the R package; Py = in the Python binding.

Signatures are the agreed ones. Three renames landed in R 0.2.0 with no deprecation aliases (the R package is pre-1.0), matching Python:

  • from / to became source / target everywhere: frames, scales, crosswalk columns, navigation, and the atom-pair columns. In recast(), the scale argument is scale and the source frame source;
  • the clear_* functions take name (registry names or keys) and scope;
  • the backend helpers .ms_* became the backend_* functions below.

A rule name may be a unique prefix ("weighted"), as with R’s match.arg(). A scoped lookup falls back to the unscoped entry. A value column with no rule (explicit or registered) is an error.

Maps

Function Arguments Returns R Py
scale_atom_pairs x, source, target, weight=NULL, ... table source, target, w (subclass hook) ✓ ✓
scale_map x, source, target, weight=NULL, by=character(), ... crosswalk ✓ ✓

get_scale_map x, source, target map, or missing ✓ ✓
get_scale_map_between source, target map, or missing ✓ ✓
list_scale_maps table key ✓ ✓
clear_scale_maps name=NULL nothing ✓ ✓

A crosswalk has columns <source label>, <target label>, n_from, n_overlap, w, w_from (plus any by columns first). n_from and n_overlap are 32-bit integers, w and w_from doubles. A missing target label marks atoms the target does not cover. The split share of sum disaggregation is w / w_from; with no weight column every atom weighs 1, so it equals n_overlap / n_from.

Attributes and aliases

Member attributes (a calorific value, an emission factor) and aliases (alternative labels) are long tables on the scale keyed by (frame, unit). Attributes are never weights and are never recast; convert_scale() applies them row by row. A kind travels with every attribute row: property is an invertible ratio, factor is one-way.

Store

Function Arguments Returns R Py

The store’s manifest is _scales/manifest.json (one definition header per axis); a legacy manifest.yaml is still read.

Definitions and catalogue

A definition is a language-neutral file: a JSON header (schema_version, class, name, key, frames, members, meta, tables, payload) with the leaftable, attribute and alias tables inline (column-wise, typed) or, in a <name>.scale/ bundle directory, as Arrow IPC or CSV files. YAML is accepted as input and optional output. The core ships carriers (fuels and energy carriers with IPCC 2006 defaults) and reads definitions from every registered directory.

Function Arguments Returns R Py
